newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen Q4 same-store sales up 8.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Walgreen Q4 same-store sales up 8.8 pct.

text.p: Walgreen Co said Monday same store sales rose 8.8 percent in the fourth quarter and were up 8.5 percent for the fiscal year.
Prescription sales in comparable stores rose 11.8 percent in the quarter and 13.0 percent for the year, despite low pharmacy inflation, it added.
L. Daniel Jorndt, president, said pharmacy sales now account for about 45 percent of total sales. Prescription sales advanced 16.9 percent for the quarter and 18.0 percent for the year.
"Walgreens -- with nearly 190 million prescriptions filled in 1996 -- is the largest and fastest growing retail prescription provider in America," Jorndt said.
He said Walgreen is rolling out an advanced pharmacy system, Intercom Plus, to speed up the prescription-filling process. Intercom Plus is expected to be in all stores by next spring.

Charles Walgreen III, chairman, said the company opened 210 new drugstores across the United States in fiscal 1996, a record. New markets for the year include Philadelphia, Dallas/Ft. Worth, Las Vegas, Portland, Ore. and Richmond, Va.
The company recently announced plans to enter two new markets by fall 1997, Detroit and Kansas City.
Walgreen said 230 new drugstores are planned for fiscal 1997 and that this aggressive expansion pace will increase during the rest of the decade.

As of August 31, Walgreen operated 2,193 stores in 34 states and Puerto Rico, compared to 2,085 a year ago. The company reiterated it expects to operate 3,000 drugstores around the country by the year 2000.
